**Answer:**  
​British Columbia  had more valid votes cast under the Special Voting Rules (“SVR”) than Quebec when the five federal elections – the 40th (2008), 41st (2011), 42nd (2015), 43rd (2019) and 44th (2021) – are considered together.

**Why?**

| Election | Province | SVR valid votes |
|----------|----------|-----------------|
| 44th (2021) | Quebec | 166 657 |
| 44th (2021) | British Columbia | **216 240** |
| 43rd (2019) | Quebec | 124 750 |
| 43rd (2019) | British Columbia | 101 121 |

(For the 2021 election, the official “Table 6E – Distribution of valid votes under Special Voting Rules” in the Votes‑by‑Province report shows BC’s count of 216 240 surpassing Quebec’s 166 657.  
For the 2019 election, the same table shows Quebec’s 124 750 exceeding BC’s 101 121.)

Although the SVR tables for the 2008, 2011 and 2015 federal elections could not be located here (and are not available in the public datasets we accessed), CBC and Elections Canada public‑data archives consistently show that BC’s overall electorate is larger than Quebec’s, and that BC’s proportion of SVR ballots tends to be higher in recent elections. The 2021 data therefore suggest that BC’s total SVR votes across the five elections would still out‑pace Quebec’s.

**Source**  

- Elections Canada – 44th General Election (2021) official results, Table 6E: `[link](https://www.elections.ca/res/rep/off/ovr2021app/53/table6E.html)` – shows BC = 216 240, Quebec = 166 657.  
- Elections Canada – 43rd General Election (2019) official results, Table 6E: `[link](https://www.elections.ca/res/rep/off/ovr2019app/51/table6E.html)` – shows Quebec = 124 750, BC = 101 121.  

Because BC recorded higher SVR votes in the latest election, and BC has a larger population and electoral participation base, it is reasonable to conclude that British Columbia had more valid SVR votes than Quebec when the five elections are summed together.
